intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.

body: The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 8.0% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Chargers get home on 8.1% (5th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chargers.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

The biggest reason? The game is at Gillette Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, NE have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Steelers score 22.4 points a game (17th in the league), and the Patriots allow 17.9 (3rd).
On a typical play the Steelers gain 4.9 yards (19th), while the Patriots give up 4.6 (6th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: On a typical play the Patriots gain 5.7 yards (3rd), while the Steelers give up 5.3 (21st).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 8.8% of dropbacks (27th), and the Steelers get home on 6.9% (10th).
So the Patriots have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Steelers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Steelers score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Steelers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.

On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 6.3 yards (2nd), while the Raiders give up 4.6 (9th).

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 74%, and it starts with their defense.

intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.

On top of that, MIN have been playing better lately.

body: The Dolphins score 12.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Vikings allow 13.7 (2nd).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bears at 56%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bears offense ranks 10th, the Falcons defense ranks 24th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bears line gives up a sack on 5.3% of dropbacks (10th), and the Falcons get home on 5.2% (24th).
The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Falcons allow 24.4 (21st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bears.

other_side.title: When the Falcons have the ball
body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.7 yards (6th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
The Falcons line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
So the Bears have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: ATL's offense is heating up.
items.text: Over the last three games, ATL have gained much more on a typical play than CHI, scoring 34 points a game to CHI's 19. That offense has been one of the best in the league right now. Expect ATL to move the ball more consistently.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Falcons are 6th in yards per play (5.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Falcons would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Falcons win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Patriots at 76%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Jets offense ranks 27th, the Patriots defense ranks 4th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Gillette Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, NE have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets score 18.6 points a game (27th in the league), and the Patriots allow 18.8 (4th).
The Jets line gives up a sack on 9.5% of dropbacks (30th), and the Patriots get home on 5.9% (19th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: The Patriots score 22.0 points a game (18th in the league), and the Jets allow 19.2 (5th).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (17th), and the Jets get home on 8.7% (5th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jets, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jets are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

line.body: The line has the Patriots by 7.5, about 75%. I'm at 76%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jets win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

On top of that, BAL have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Ravens gain 5.9 yards (4th), while the Bengals give up 5.2 (22nd).
The Ravens line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (18th), and the Bengals get home on 9.3% (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Ravens.

other_side.title: When the Bengals have the ball
body: The Bengals line gives up a sack on 4.5% of dropbacks (7th), and the Ravens get home on 5.2% (23rd).
The Bengals score 25.6 points a game (10th in the league), and the Ravens allow 23.8 (20th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bengals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bengals are 10th in points per game (25.6). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bengals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Ravens have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bengals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

The biggest reason? Over the last three games, KC have gained much more on a typical play than DEN, scoring 29 points a game to DEN's 22. That offense has been one of the best in the league right now. Expect KC to move the ball more consistently.
On top of that, division game.

body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 6.3 yards (1st), while the Broncos give up 5.0 (17th).

So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Broncos would erase most of the edge I just described.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? The game is at Bernabeu, a neutral site, but my model still gives ATL the standard home-team bump of about 6.5 points of win chance.
On top of that, ATL have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Falcons line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Bengals get home on 9.3% (1st).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bengals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

other_side.title: When the Bengals have the ball
body: The Bengals line gives up a sack on 4.5% of dropbacks (7th), and the Falcons get home on 5.2% (24th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bengals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bengals are 10th in points per game (25.6). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Falcons have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bengals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Packers at 52%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Vikings offense ranks 24th, the Packers defense ranks 7th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at Lambeau Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, gB's offense is heating up.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Vikings gain 4.4 yards (24th), while the Packers give up 4.5 (7th).
The Vikings line gives up a sack on 9.1% of dropbacks (28th), and the Packers get home on 7.0% (13th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Packers.

other_side.title: When the Packers have the ball
body: The Packers score 20.8 points a game (24th in the league), and the Vikings allow 12.8 (1st).
On a typical play the Packers gain 5.2 yards (12th), while the Vikings give up 4.2 (3rd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Vikings, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: MIN have been playing better lately.
items.text: MIN are 3-0 over their last three games; GB are 2-1. They also have about 5 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Vikings are 1st in points allowed per game (12.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Vikings would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Vikings score 14 or more in the first half, the Packers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Vikings win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Packers win about 52 of them. That means the Vikings win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Vikings win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

On top of that, KC are at home.

body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 6.3 yards (1st), while the Cardinals give up 5.7 (30th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball

So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: ARI's defense has been tougher.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 59%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bills offense ranks 3rd, the Dolphins defense ranks 26th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? The game is at Highmark Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BUF have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bills gain 6.1 yards (3rd), while the Dolphins give up 5.5 (26th).
The Bills score 31.8 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Dolphins allow 26.4 (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Dolphins have the ball
body: The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Bills get home on 6.0% (18th).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 59% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 59 of them. That means the Dolphins win 41, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chargers at 53%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Jets offense ranks 30th, the Chargers defense ranks 9th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 9.5% of dropbacks (30th), and the Chargers get home on 7.3% (9th).
On a typical play the Jets gain 4.5 yards (22nd), while the Chargers give up 4.7 (10th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chargers.

other_side.title: When the Chargers have the ball
body: The Chargers line gives up a sack on 9.9% of dropbacks (31st), and the Jets get home on 8.7% (5th).
The Chargers score 16.8 points a game (30th in the league), and the Jets allow 19.2 (5th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jets, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: NYJ have been playing better lately.
items.text: NYJ are 1-2 over their last three games; LAC are 0-3. They also have about 3 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jets are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Chargers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chargers win about 53 of them. That means the Jets win 47, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jets win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Cowboys at 59%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Cowboys offense ranks 2nd, the Titans defense ranks 17th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? The game is at AT&T Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, DAL have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Cowboys line gives up a sack on 2.7% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Titans get home on 6.1% (17th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Cowboys.

other_side.title: When the Titans have the ball
body: The Titans line gives up a sack on 5.7% of dropbacks (16th), and the Cowboys get home on 3.1% (30th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Titans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 11th in points allowed per game (21.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Cowboys have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 59% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Cowboys win about 59 of them. That means the Titans win 41, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Patriots at 56%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Chargers offense ranks 30th, the Patriots defense ranks 4th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? NE are 2-1 over their last three games; LAC are 0-3. They also have about 8 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, rest tilts toward NE.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Chargers score 16.8 points a game (30th in the league), and the Patriots allow 18.8 (4th).
On a typical play the Chargers gain 4.2 yards (29th), while the Patriots give up 4.8 (12th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: The Patriots line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (17th), and the Chargers get home on 7.3% (9th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Chargers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Chargers are 10th in yards per play allowed (4.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Chargers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chargers score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Chargers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 56% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Patriots win about 56 of them. That means the Chargers win 44, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Chargers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Jaguars at 59%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Titans offense ranks 32nd, the Jaguars defense ranks 2nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? JAX are 3-0 over their last three games; TEN are 0-3. They also have about 23 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, JAX are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Titans score 11.6 points a game (32nd in the league), and the Jaguars allow 14.0 (2nd).
On a typical play the Titans gain 4.2 yards (32nd), while the Jaguars give up 5.1 (19th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Jaguars.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: The Jaguars line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (19th), and the Titans get home on 6.1% (17th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Titans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 11th in points allowed per game (21.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Jaguars defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 59% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Jaguars win about 59 of them. That means the Titans win 41, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 57%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Panthers offense ranks 14th, the Vikings defense ranks 4th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at U.S. Bank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, MIN have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Panthers line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (14th), and the Vikings get home on 9.1% (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings score 21.8 points a game (20th in the league), and the Panthers allow 27.2 (27th).
On paper this side of the ball is a wash, so I'm not leaning on it either way.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Panthers are 4th in points per game (30.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Panthers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Panthers score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Panthers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 57% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Vikings win about 57 of them. That means the Panthers win 43, which is a lot.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.7 yards (6th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (25th).
The Falcons line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Lions get home on 8.0% (6th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Falcons.

other_side.title: When the Lions have the ball

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Lions, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

On top of that, rest tilts toward CHI.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jaguars line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (19th), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
On a typical play the Jaguars gain 5.2 yards (13th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bears.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Jaguars score 14 or more in the first half, the Bears defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

body: The Dolphins score 14.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Broncos allow 22.2 (14th).

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the Broncos defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 60% actually means

clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Commanders offense ranks 19th, the Titans defense ranks 13th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at Nissan Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Commanders gain 4.8 yards (19th), while the Titans give up 4.9 (13th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Titans.

other_side.title: When the Titans have the ball
body: The Titans line gives up a sack on 5.7% of dropbacks (16th), and the Commanders get home on 4.7% (26th).
On a typical play the Titans gain 4.2 yards (32nd), while the Commanders give up 5.3 (24th).
On paper this side of the ball is a wash, so I'm not leaning on it either way.

items.lead: WAS have been playing better lately.
items.text: WAS are 1-2 over their last three games; TEN are 0-3. They also have about 6 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Commanders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Commanders score 14 or more in the first half, the Titans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Commanders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Titans win about 52 of them. That means the Commanders win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Commanders win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bears at 52%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Dolphins offense ranks 29th, the Bears defense ranks 2nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? CHI are 2-1 over their last three games; MIA are 0-3. They also have about 11 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
The Dolphins score 14.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Bears allow 19.2 (5th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bears.

other_side.title: When the Bears have the ball
body: The Bears line gives up a sack on 5.3% of dropbacks (10th), and the Dolphins get home on 1.9% (32nd).
The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Dolphins allow 26.4 (24th).
So the Bears have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the Bears defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bears win about 52 of them. That means the Dolphins win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Colts at 51%, and it starts with their offense.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? IND are 2-1 over their last three games; PHI are 0-3. They also have about 11 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, rest tilts toward IND.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Colts line gives up a sack on 4.7% of dropbacks (8th), and the Eagles get home on 3.5% (28th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Colts.

other_side.title: When the Eagles have the ball
body: On a typical play the Eagles gain 4.3 yards (26th), while the Colts give up 5.8 (31st).
So the Colts have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Eagles would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Colts have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Eagles win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 51% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Colts win about 51 of them. That means the Eagles win 49, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Eagles win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the 49ers at 54%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the 49ers offense ranks 1st, the Rams defense ranks 22nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? The game is at Levi's Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, SF have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The 49ers line gives up a sack on 1.7% of dropbacks (1st), and the Rams get home on 5.3% (22nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the Rams have the ball
body: The Rams score 21.2 points a game (23rd in the league), and the 49ers allow 18.6 (3rd).
The Rams line gives up a sack on 3.0% of dropbacks (3rd), and the 49ers get home on 6.5% (15th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Rams are 1st in yards per play allowed (3.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Rams would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Rams win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 54% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the 49ers win about 54 of them. That means the Rams win 46, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Rams win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 61%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Titans offense ranks 16th, the Lions defense ranks 6th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? DET are 2-1 over their last three games; TEN are 0-3. They also have about 20 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, DET are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Titans line gives up a sack on 5.7% of dropbacks (16th), and the Lions get home on 8.0% (6th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Lions have the ball
body: The Lions score 32.8 points a game (1st in the league), and the Titans allow 21.8 (11th).
So the Lions have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 11th in points allowed per game (21.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Lions defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 61% actually means

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 56%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bills offense ranks 3rd, the Bears defense ranks 27th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at Highmark Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BUF have the better scoring margin.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bills gain 6.1 yards (3rd), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
The Bills line gives up a sack on 6.8% of dropbacks (21st), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Bears have the ball
body: The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Bills allow 26.8 (25th).
The Bears line gives up a sack on 5.3% of dropbacks (10th), and the Bills get home on 6.0% (18th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bears, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bears are 5th in points allowed per game (19.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bears would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bears win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 56% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 56 of them. That means the Bears win 44, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bears win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 52%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Jets offense ranks 27th, the Vikings defense ranks 1st. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? MIN are 3-0 over their last three games; NYJ are 1-2. They also have about 12 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets score 18.6 points a game (27th in the league), and the Vikings allow 12.8 (1st).
The Jets line gives up a sack on 9.5% of dropbacks (30th), and the Vikings get home on 9.1% (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings line gives up a sack on 9.1% of dropbacks (28th), and the Jets get home on 8.7% (5th).
On a typical play the Vikings gain 4.4 yards (24th), while the Jets give up 4.2 (4th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jets, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: MIN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for NYJ in this game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jets are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the 49ers at 56%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the 49ers offense ranks 3rd, the Cardinals defense ranks 32nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? SF are 3-0 over their last three games; ARI are 0-3. They also have about 20 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The 49ers score 30.8 points a game (3rd in the league), and the Cardinals allow 32.4 (32nd).
On a typical play the 49ers gain 6.3 yards (2nd), while the Cardinals give up 5.7 (30th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.2 yards (31st), while the 49ers give up 4.3 (5th).
The Cardinals score 21.6 points a game (22nd in the league), and the 49ers allow 18.6 (3rd).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: SF's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for ARI in this game.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 56% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the 49ers win about 56 of them. That means the Cardinals win 44, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
